title: The Person Isn't Here
evidence_boundary: Emerging: predictive processing and theory-of-mind research support the idea that people build working models of others. This script does not claim another person's actions are imaginary or that real harm should be dismissed.
grounding: The closing beats return the viewer to their own room and breath.
invitation: Picture the person you resent, remove every sentence you supplied for them, and notice what remains.
end_card_question: What remains when you question the render?
voice_standard: Liam - warm, sly, a brilliant friend at midnight; spacious and intimate through the turn, near-whisper on the closing question.

scenes.text: You have never argued with another person. Not exactly. You argued with the version your mind assembled.

scenes.query: two chairs facing each other across a warm table, one occupied and one empty, slow camera push through moving window light

scenes.text: I know how that sounds—like I’m excusing them and blaming your imagination. I’m not.
scenes.primary_symbol: a judge's wooden gavel resting untouched beside balanced sca
scenes.query: a judge's wooden gavel resting untouched beside balanced scales while sunlight shifts across the desk

scenes.text: Harm is real. Words land. Choices leave bruises you cannot meditate into confetti.
scenes.primary_symbol: a falling wooden block strikes a ceramic cup and sends it sl
scenes.query: a falling wooden block strikes a ceramic cup and sends it sliding across a brightly side-lit table

scenes.text: The person who hurt you is not stored in your head as a complete human.
scenes.primary_symbol: hands sort partial portrait photographs into illuminated arc
scenes.query: hands sort partial portrait photographs into illuminated archive drawers as the camera tracks sideways

scenes.text: Your mind keeps fragments: a tone, a slammed door, three texts, the face before “fine.”
scenes.primary_symbol: a moving film contact sheet alternates between a closing doo
scenes.query: a moving film contact sheet alternates between a closing door, glowing phone, voice recorder, and frozen expression

scenes.text: Then it opens an animation studio and fills in the missing footage.
scenes.primary_symbol: macro view of sprockets pulling celluloid through mechanical
scenes.query: macro view of sprockets pulling celluloid through mechanical rollers beneath a warm moving work light

scenes.text: It guesses motives, predicts dialogue, adjusts the lighting, and adds a suspicious soundtrack.
scenes.primary_symbol: a mechanical metronome swings beside rotating cinema lights
scenes.query: a mechanical metronome swings beside rotating cinema lights and a pulsing analog waveform meter

scenes.text: Psychology calls part of this theory of mind: building models of people so you can navigate them.
scenes.primary_symbol: a researcher studies animated paths connecting faces and ges
scenes.query: a researcher studies animated paths connecting faces and gestures on a transparent display in a bright modern lab

scenes.text: What remains emerging is how strongly prediction shapes who you experience in real time.
scenes.primary_symbol: a road seen through a windshield changes focus from a projec
scenes.query: a road seen through a windshield changes focus from a projected route overlay to the real moving traffic ahead

scenes.text: So when you replay the argument at two in the morning, they are not actually there.
scenes.primary_symbol: an illuminated bedside clock reads two in the morning while
scenes.query: an illuminated bedside clock reads two in the morning while an empty chair rocks slightly near rain-streaked curtains

scenes.text: You are debating a character rendered from evidence, memory, fear, and your nervous system’s “previously on...”
scenes.primary_symbol: a film editor scrubs rapidly through scattered clips on a la
scenes.query: a film editor scrubs rapidly through scattered clips on a large monitor while red timeline markers pulse

scenes.text: That is why your opponent always says the worst possible thing. Committed actor. Terrible union rules.
scenes.primary_symbol: a wind-up theater puppet gestures dramatically beneath a mov
scenes.query: a wind-up theater puppet gestures dramatically beneath a moving spotlight while tiny curtains flutter

scenes.text: Here is the uncomfortable turn: they are doing the same thing to you.
scenes.primary_symbol: two security cameras rotate toward each other in a well-lit
scenes.query: two security cameras rotate toward each other in a well-lit corridor, each filling the other's monitor

scenes.text: Somewhere, a version of you lives inside someone else’s editing room, saying lines you never approved.
scenes.primary_symbol: two neighboring editing suites seen through glass, each edit
scenes.query: two neighboring editing suites seen through glass, each editor cutting a different version of the same figure

scenes.text: Neither model is nonsense. Each is built from real footage.
scenes.primary_symbol: authentic documentary film strips travel through a projector
scenes.query: authentic documentary film strips travel through a projector and cast moving everyday scenes onto a white wall

scenes.text: But footage is not a whole life. A camera angle can be accurate and incomplete.
scenes.primary_symbol: a camera circles a sculpture, revealing a different shape wi
scenes.query: a camera circles a sculpture, revealing a different shape with every smoothly changing angle

scenes.text: The character is not the person. It is the loading screen your mind built from fragments.
scenes.primary_symbol: an old arcade screen loads portrait fragments one by one whi
scenes.query: an old arcade screen loads portrait fragments one by one while its progress bar advances in warm neon light

scenes.text: That does not mean reopening a dangerous door or pretending harm was love.
scenes.primary_symbol: a solid apartment door closes and its deadbolt turns while s
scenes.query: a solid apartment door closes and its deadbolt turns while soft morning light remains visible through nearby windows

scenes.text: You can keep the boundary without turning your render into a prison.

scenes.query: window-blind shadows resembling bars slide away from an editing monitor as the room fills with daylight

scenes.text: Maybe they were cruel. Maybe you misread one piece. Maybe both are true.

scenes.query: two transparent film frames overlap above balanced scales, both images remaining visible as the beam settles

scenes.text: Mercy is not deleting evidence. It is labeling missing footage “missing.”

scenes.query: a reel of developed film moves past several clean empty frames without stopping or being cut

scenes.text: Look around the room. Feel your jaw. Lower your shoulders. Notice who is actually here.

scenes.query: a person relaxes their jaw and shoulders in a sunlit living room as curtains move gently and a kettle steams

scenes.text: What remains—and what might change if you questioned the render without abandoning what happened?
